VAR-psu.why: Grain includes psu; rt001.psu is labeled Primary Sampling Unit and is a key identifier.
Also present as a key identifier on the person roster (rt002), confirming psu is carried across files.

VAR-strata.why: Likely sampling stratum; column named stratum with 16 distinct values in the household-level file.

VAR-subnatid1.why: Highest admin unit available at household level: Division (region) in rt001.

VAR-subnatid2.why: Household-level district code (rt001.district) is a plausible second-level admin identifier.

VAR-subnatid3.why: Household-level Upazila/Thana code (rt001.thana) is a plausible third-level admin identifier.

VAR-subnatid4.why: Household-level union code (rt001.union) is a plausible fourth-level admin identifier.

VAR-subnatidsurvey.why: Most granular explicit location code in the household file appears to be Mouza Code (rt001.mouza); candidate for lowest-level subnational id used for crosswalks.
If mouza is not the survey's lowest standardized admin unit, union code (rt001.union) is an alternate candidate for the lowest-level subnational id.

VAR-geocode.why: Resolved geocode is derived from the survey's lowest available subnational id; start from mouza (or union) to build a crosswalk to the resolved geocode.

VAR-gauladm1code.why: GAUL admin codes are derived from the resolved geocode; the survey-side anchor is the lowest-level location code (mouza/union) used to construct VAR-geocode.

VAR-gauladm2code.why: GAUL admin codes are derived from the resolved geocode; the survey-side anchor is the lowest-level location code (mouza/union) used to construct VAR-geocode.

VAR-subnatid1prev.why: Previous subnational IDs are derived from VAR-geocode; the survey-side anchor for building geocode is the lowest-level location code (mouza/union).
